funFact: A 1920 US Cavalry manual said a horse should carry no more than about a fifth of its own weight, which is roughly one rider and a saddle.
No ancient writer recorded the horse's weight, so this one is our estimate: a hollow timber horse plus 30 soldiers in bronze armor.
A big mosasaurus weighed about 10 tons, and it was no dinosaur: it belonged to the same reptile group as today's lizards and snakes.
Gigantopithecus was the largest ape that ever lived. It is known only from teeth and jaws, which point to an animal as heavy as three people.
A fully loaded 747 weighs over 400 tons, and about 40% of that can be fuel.
